ev.eur_m_bells.text: The bells ring for matins, for Mass, for vespers. You have learned to tell the time by them like the grown-ups: when to get up, when to eat, when to run home.
ev.eur_m_lent_herring.text: Forty days of Lent: no meat, no lard, no eggs. You dream of the salt herring on the table, and by Easter you would give anything for a slice of ham.
ev.eur_m_carnival.text: The last day before Lent: mummers in masks, flour-bag fights, a pig roasted in the square and noise till midnight. Tomorrow there will be ashes on your brow, but tonight anything goes.
ev.eur_m_mystery_play.text: On the cathedral steps the carpenters' guild performs the play of Noah's Ark. Noah quarrels with his stubborn wife, the crowd roars with laughter, and then real water pours from above.
ev.eur_m_paris_bridge.text: On the Grand-Pont over the Seine the money-changers sit at their tables: coins from Flanders, England and Italy ring. Below, the water roars around the mill wheels, and overhead stand houses built right on the bridge.
ev.eur_m_paris_students.text: On the Left Bank the students have brawled with the townsfolk again over a jug of wine. Half the quarter argues in Latin, the other half swears in French.
ev.eur_m_london_skates.text: The marsh outside the city wall has frozen. You tie sheep bones to your feet and race across the ice, pushing with a stick – faster than a bird, until you land on your nose.
ev.eur_m_london_bridge.text: Stone London Bridge is a whole street above the Thames: shops, houses, the chapel of Saint Thomas. Under its arches the water roars so hard that boatmen fear to shoot it at ebb tide.
ev.eur_m_florence_dyers.text: The dyers empty their vats straight into the Arno, and the river runs in streaks of blue and crimson. It smells of alum and urine, but kings wear cloth from these vats.
ev.eur_m_florence_towers.text: Dozens of stone towers belonging to great families bristle over Florence. Bridges are thrown between them, and in times of feud stones and arrows fly from the top. You keep clear of other families' towers.
ev.eur_m_cologne_shrine.text: Pilgrims from all over Europe come to the golden shrine of the Three Kings. You queue with Flemings and Hungarians and think: the very Magi who followed the star now lie here, in Cologne.
ev.eur_m_cologne_crane.text: A huge wooden crane stands on the unfinished cathedral: men walk inside its wheel to lift the stone. They say the cathedral takes longer to build than a man lives, and you begin to believe it.
ev.eur_m_toledo_three_faiths.text: In the evening in Toledo the cathedral bell rings, the Jewish quarter sings its Sabbath prayer, and from the Moorish quarter comes the call to prayer. Three faiths within one wall.
ev.eur_m_toledo_swords.text: A swordsmith by the Alcántara bridge quenches a blade in the waters of the Tagus. The steel hisses, and the master shows you how it bends almost into a ring – and springs straight again.
ev.eur_m_haymaking.text: Haymaking: the whole village is in the meadow from dawn till dark. Scythes ring, the girls turn the hay with rakes, and at night everyone drinks ale beside the stack.
ev.eur_m_pig_slaughter.text: November, Martinmas: the pig fattened on acorns all autumn is slaughtered. Sausages, lard and ham go up into the smoke – for the whole winter. For the first time you helped with the salting.
ev.eur_m_bean_king.text: On Twelfth Night a cake is baked with a bean inside. The bean was in your slice – and until morning you are the King of the Bean, in a paper crown, with everyone drinking your health.
ev.eur_m_saint_john.text: On Midsummer Eve the bonfires of Saint John are lit, and the young people leap the flames in pairs – the higher the jump, the luckier the year. You leapt and did not even singe your hem.
ev.eur_m_champagne_fair.text: At the fair in Troyes Lombards change money, Flemings lay out cloth and merchants from Genoa sell pepper and saffron. All Europe in one field, haggling in a jumble of tongues.
ev.eur_m_relics.text: On the patron saint's day the reliquary is carried round the church. You squeezed through the crowd and touched the carved casket. They say it keeps fever away.
ev.eur_m_stained_glass.text: Sunlight pours through the stained glass of the new cathedral, laying patches of blue and red on the stone floor. You stand among them as if inside a jewel.
ev.eur_m_scriptorium.text: An old monk showed you a manuscript: initials in gold leaf, and in the margin a hare riding a snail. He laughs: "Scribes get bored too."
ev.eur_m_falconry.text: Falconry: the falcon leaves the glove, climbs and drops like a stone onto a heron. The falconer says this bird is worth more than a village.
ev.eur_m_tournament_watch.text: A tournament in the meadow outside town: heralds cry the arms, horses in trappers, lances shattering. One knight is thrown from the saddle right by the barrier where you stand – and gets up, to the crowd's delight.
ev.eur_m_bathhouse.text: The bathhouse down the street blows its horn in the morning: the water is hot! Steam, wooden tubs, the attendant with his switch of twigs – and all the neighbourhood news for one coin.
ev.eur_m_alestake.text: The bush is hanging over the widow's door across the road again: fresh ale has been brewed. By evening half the village is on her bench.
ev.eur_m_wolves.text: The winter is snowy, and at night wolves howl at the edge of the village. The animals are brought indoors, the doors are barred, and you lie awake a long time, listening.
ev.eur_m_lords_mill.text: Grain may be ground only at the lord's mill, and the miller keeps one measure in sixteen. Hand mills at home are forbidden – the neighbour's were smashed last autumn.
ev.eur_m_tithe_barn.text: Every tenth sheaf goes to the Church. The collector counts them right there in the field and marks them. The tithe cart creaks off to the great barn by the monastery.
ev.eur_m_troubadour.text: A troubadour sings in the hall – of a lady who must not be loved, and a knight who loves her all the same. The ladies sigh; the knights pretend to be bored.
ev.eur_m_spectacles.text: The letters have been blurring for years. A craftsman from Pisa sold you glass lenses in a bone frame that sit on your nose. The world is sharp again – and you can read in the evenings.
ev.eur_m_clock.text: A mechanical clock has been set up on the tower. It strikes every hour, day and night, the same for monk and merchant. The old folk grumble that time now belongs to the town.
ev.eur_m_olive_harvest.text: November: the olives are beaten down with sticks onto cloths spread beneath the trees. Fingers freeze, but the press smells of new oil, and the first bread dipped in it is sweeter than honey.
ev.eur_m_vintage.text: The grape harvest: baskets, sticky hands, wasps. Children tread the grapes in the vat while the old men taste last year's wine and argue this one will be better.
ev.eur_m_printed_book.text: At a bookseller's you saw a book made not by pen but by press: hundreds of identical pages, even lines, not a single blot. It costs a fraction of a handwritten one.
ev.eur_m_shabbat.text: Friday at sunset: two candles are lit on the table, the challah lies under an embroidered cloth. For one day all the noise of the city stays outside the door – it is the Sabbath.
ev.eur_m_ramadan_toledo.text: Ramadan in the Moorish quarter: not a crumb all day, then after sunset dates, chickpea soup and talk on the rooftops late into the night. Your Castilian neighbours peer in, curious about the feast.
ev.eur_m_plough_team.text: For the first time you are trusted with the heavy plough. Eight oxen shared by four families, the furrow vanishing into the mist – and you must keep it straight, or be mocked until Easter.
ev.eur_m_spinning_evening.text: A winter evening: the women gather in one cottage with their distaffs to save on rushlights. Spindles hum, and the gossip about the miller flies faster than the thread.
ev.eur_d_corvee.title: Labour service at harvest
ev.eur_d_corvee.text: The lord's steward demands two more days on the demesne – just as your own grain is ripe and shedding, and clouds are rolling in from the west.
ev.eur_d_corvee.own_first: Bring in your own first, then go
ev.eur_d_corvee.own_first.success: The steward was busy and noticed nothing. Your grain is in the barn.
ev.eur_d_corvee.own_first.failure: The steward noticed. A fine in the manor court and sidelong looks.
ev.eur_d_corvee.court: Complain to the manor court with your neighbours
ev.eur_d_corvee.court.success: The jurors confirmed that by custom harvest service is no more than three days. The steward backed down.
ev.eur_d_corvee.court.failure: The lord's court ruled for the lord. Who could have doubted it.
ev.eur_d_merchet.title: The marriage fine
ev.eur_d_merchet.text: You want to marry a lad from the neighbouring manor. But a serf woman may not marry without her lord's leave: there is a fine to pay, and double if the bride leaves for another village.
ev.eur_d_merchet.steward: Marry the man the steward picks
ev.eur_d_merchet.flee: Run away together to the town
ev.eur_d_merchet.flee.success: You reached the town and found day labour. A year and a day – and you are both free.
ev.eur_d_merchet.flee.failure: You were caught at the ford. He was sent back to his manor, you to the steward.
ev.eur_d_merchet_later.title: The lord's man
ev.eur_d_merchet_later.text: Years later your old lord's bailiff recognised you in the town. He shouts down the street that you are a runaway serf and must go back.
ev.eur_d_merchet_later.charter: Call the town elders: the town's liberties are on your side
ev.eur_d_merchet_later.charter.success: The elders confirmed it: whoever has lived in the town a year and a day is free. The bailiff left empty-handed.
ev.eur_d_merchet_later.charter.failure: The elders did not want a quarrel with a lord. You had to buy your freedom.
ev.eur_d_apprentice.title: Apprenticeship
ev.eur_d_apprentice.text: A guild master on the next street will take you as an apprentice for seven years: bed and board, not a coin of pay, and a fee for the indenture. But after that – a trade for life.
ev.eur_d_masterpiece.title: The masterpiece
ev.eur_d_masterpiece.text: Your years of training are behind you. To become a master you must present the guild with a masterpiece – your finest work – and pay for a feast for the wardens.
ev.eur_d_masterpiece.make.success: The wardens turned the piece over in their hands, nodded – and admitted you as a master.
ev.eur_d_masterpiece.make.failure: The wardens found a flaw. The feast is eaten, and you are still a journeyman.
ev.eur_d_masterpiece.widow: Court the late master's widow – the workshop comes with her
ev.eur_d_pilgrimage.title: The road to Saint James
ev.eur_d_pilgrimage.text: Your neighbours are setting off for Santiago de Compostela, to the tomb of the Apostle James: a scallop shell on the hat, a staff, months of walking and nights in pilgrim hostels. They ask you to come.
ev.eur_d_pilgrimage.text.toledo: Pilgrims pass through Toledo on their way to Santiago de Compostela, to the tomb of the Apostle James. Your neighbours are going too: a shell on the hat, a staff, months of walking north. They ask you to come.
ev.eur_d_pilgrimage.donate: Give money for a candle at the tomb
ev.eur_d_pilgrim_later.title: A fellow pilgrim
ev.eur_d_pilgrim_later.text: At the door is the man you once shared bread with on the road to Compostela. He is a trader now and offers you a share in his business.
ev.eur_d_pilgrim_later.partner.success: Saint James clearly remembers his own: the goods sold at a profit.
ev.eur_d_pilgrim_later.partner.failure: The goods got stuck at a toll. The money is gone, the friendship remains.
ev.eur_d_pilgrim_later.host: Simply welcome him as a guest and remember the road
ev.eur_d_university.title: The university
ev.eur_d_university.text: You could go and study the liberal arts: lectures in Latin from dawn, straw on the floor instead of benches, disputes about Aristotle and constant hunger. But a master of arts can become anything.
ev.eur_d_university.text.paris: On the Left Bank of the Seine the masters lecture in Latin from dawn: straw instead of benches, disputes about Aristotle, constant hunger. To enrol in the university is to become a clerk and a scholar.
ev.eur_d_university.text.london: You could go to study at Oxford: lectures in Latin, disputes about Aristotle, brawls with the townsfolk and constant hunger. But a master of arts can become anything.
ev.eur_d_university.text.florence: You could go to Bologna, where all Europe comes to study law: lectures in Latin, Justinian's code, disputes and constant hunger. But a doctor of law can become anything.
ev.eur_d_university.text.toledo: You could go to study at Salamanca: lectures in Latin, disputes about Aristotle and his Arab commentators, constant hunger. But a master of arts can become anything.
ev.eur_d_university_later.title: Master of arts
ev.eur_d_university_later.text: You passed your disputation and took the degree of master. Several roads lie before you.
ev.eur_d_university_later.chancery: Enter the chancery as a clerk
ev.eur_d_tithe.title: The small tithe
ev.eur_d_tithe.text: The rector's collector demands a tithe not only on grain but on lambs, the garden and even eggs. He says it was always so. The old folk say it was not.
ev.eur_d_tithe.hide: Hide some lambs with the neighbours
ev.eur_d_tithe.hide.success: The collector counted fewer and left satisfied.
ev.eur_d_tithe.hide.failure: Someone informed. You had to hand over everything and pay a fine, and from the pulpit you were called a thief of God's goods.
ev.eur_d_tithe.appeal.success: The bishop's court upheld the old custom. The collector had to curb his appetite.
ev.eur_d_tithe.appeal.failure: The case dragged on for a year and cost more than the tithe itself.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.title: Trial by ordeal
ev.eur_d_ordeal.text: A neighbour accuses you of stealing a pig. The court offers the judgement of God: carry a red-hot iron nine paces. If the wound is clean after three days, you are innocent. Or find twelve men who will swear for you.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.iron.success: After three days the bandage came off – the wound was clean. The neighbour begged forgiveness before everyone.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.iron.failure: The wound festered. You were found guilty: a fine, disgrace and a palm that took long to heal.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.oath.success: Twelve neighbours swore on the relics to your honesty. The charge was dropped.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.oath.failure: The eleventh stumbled over the words of the oath at the last moment. So you are guilty.
ev.eur_d_ordeal.pay: Pay for the pig and be done with it
ev.eur_d_crusade_vow.title: Taking the cross
ev.eur_d_crusade_vow.text: A preacher in the square calls men to march for the Holy Sepulchre. Whoever takes the cross is forgiven all his sins, and his debts are frozen until he returns. Men around you are sewing red crosses to their shoulders.
ev.eur_d_crusade_vow.take.success: You came back from overseas sunburnt and scarred, with plunder and stories to last a lifetime.
ev.eur_d_crusade_vow.take.failure: The expedition turned into disease and defeat. You came home barely alive and without a penny.
ev.eur_d_crusader_return.title: From overseas
ev.eur_d_crusader_return.text: Years have passed, yet in the tavern they still ask you to tell of Acre, camels and Saracen physicians. In your chest lies a splinter sold to you in the Holy Land as a piece of the True Cross.
ev.eur_d_crusader_return.stories: Tell the truth, whatever it was
ev.eur_d_crusader_return.relic.success: The abbot received the splinter reverently and paid handsomely.
ev.eur_d_crusader_return.relic.failure: The sacristan recognised an ordinary cedar shaving. Disgrace across the whole district.
ev.eur_d_convent.title: The dowry
ev.eur_d_convent.text: The family council is deciding your fate: gather a dowry for a good match, or make a gift to a convent – that costs less, and the life is quiet, with books and prayer.
ev.eur_d_usury.title: Money at interest
ev.eur_d_usury.text: You need money for seed and tools. The Church forbids Christians to lend at interest, but by the bridge a Lombard sits at his bench: he will lend as much as you need, and what you owe back is written in small letters.
ev.eur_d_usury_later.title: The debt falls due
ev.eur_d_usury_later.text: The Lombard has come with a notary and a document: over the years the debt has nearly doubled. "That isn't interest," he smiles, "it's payment for my risk."
ev.eur_d_usury_later.plead: Threaten him with the Church court for usury
ev.eur_d_usury_later.plead.success: The Lombard had no wish to explain himself to the bishop and took only the principal.
ev.eur_d_usury_later.plead.failure: The Lombard had friends at the bishop's court. You had to pay the judge as well.
ev.eur_d_heretic_preacher.title: The good men
ev.eur_d_heretic_preacher.text: A pale man in black speaks by the well: the priests are rich and sinful, the world was made by evil, and true Christians live in poverty, eat no meat and swear no oaths. People listen, glancing over their shoulders.
ev.eur_d_inquisitor_later.title: Questions
ev.eur_d_inquisitor_later.text: The bishop's investigator is going round the district asking who went to hear the preacher in black. Someone has already named you.
ev.eur_d_inquisitor_later.deny.success: The investigator believed you: plenty of people stood by the well.
ev.eur_d_inquisitor_later.deny.failure: Witnesses were found. You were ordered to wear a sewn-on yellow cross and pay a heavy fine.
ev.eur_d_inquisitor_later.name: Name others so they let you go
ev.eur_d_pardoner.title: The pardoner
ev.eur_d_pardoner.text: In the market a pardoner unrolls sealed letters and shows a little glass reliquary: "A bone of Saint Peter! One kiss and a hundred days off purgatory."
ev.eur_d_pardoner.mock: Ask loudly why the bone smells of pork
ev.eur_d_pardoner.mock.success: The crowd roars, and the pardoner hastily packs up his stall.
ev.eur_d_pardoner.mock.failure: Pious old women hissed at you, and the pardoner promised you excommunication.
ev.eur_d_poaching.title: The king's forest
ev.eur_d_poaching.text: The winter is hungry, and beyond the stream begins the king's forest. The deer there are unafraid, but the king's foresters punish men for less – ever since the Normans declared the forest the king's preserve.
ev.eur_d_poaching.poach: Go at night with a bow
ev.eur_d_poaching.poach.success: Venison on the table all week, the bones buried under the hearth.
ev.eur_d_poaching.poach.failure: The foresters caught you by the stream. The forest court, a huge fine and the name of poacher.
ev.eur_d_poaching.rabbits: Set snares for rabbits on the common
ev.eur_d_mezzadria.title: Sharecropping
ev.eur_d_mezzadria.text: A Florentine merchant has bought up land around and offers you a farm on halves: the house, oxen and seed are his, and the harvest is split down the middle. Your own patch of land is exhausted.
ev.eur_d_mezzadria.own: Hold on to your own plot
ev.eur_d_mezzadria.city: Go to the city as a wool carder
ev.eur_d_guelf.title: Guelfs and Ghibellines
ev.eur_d_guelf.text: The city is split: the Guelfs stand for the Pope, the Ghibellines for the Emperor – and in truth for their own towers and grudges. Today at the guild they asked you outright which side you are on.
ev.eur_d_guelf.neutral: With no one: business comes first
ev.eur_d_faction_later.title: The exile lists
ev.eur_d_faction_later.text: The other party has won. Lists of exiles hang on the doors of the Signoria, and your name is on them. Your house may be pulled down and your goods taken for the treasury.
ev.eur_d_faction_later.exile: Go into exile until the wind changes
ev.eur_d_tournament.title: The tournament
ev.eur_d_tournament.text: The heralds have proclaimed a tournament. The victor takes the loser's horse and armour, the loser pays a ransom. The ladies are already handing out sleeves to tie on lances.
ev.eur_d_tournament.joust.success: You unhorsed your opponent with the first stroke. His horse is yours now.
ev.eur_d_tournament.joust.failure: A blow to the helm – and you came to on the grass. The ransom for your horse and armour will eat half a year's income.
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.title: A loan for the count
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.text: The count asks you for a large sum for his campaign. Refusing a powerful man is dangerous: the whole community depends on his protection. Lending may mean never seeing the money again.
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.lend.success: The count came back with plunder and repaid with interest.
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.lend.failure: The count declared that debts to Jews were void. The king did not object.
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.refuse.success: The count shrugged and found another lender.
ev.eur_d_jewish_loan.refuse.failure: The count bore a grudge: a new levy was suddenly laid on your shop.
ev.eur_d_sumptuary.title: Above your station
ev.eur_d_sumptuary.text: A town officer stops you in the street: squirrel fur on the collar and long-toed shoes are forbidden to townsfolk of your rank. Those are for knights.
ev.eur_d_sumptuary.argue: Argue: the fur was bought with honest money
ev.eur_d_sumptuary.argue.success: The officer waved you off. Later the neighbours asked where you bought such fur.
ev.eur_d_sumptuary.argue.failure: The fine was doubled and the fur cut off right there in the street.
ev.eur_d_boundary.title: The boundary
ev.eur_d_boundary.text: At ploughing time your neighbour has again taken a furrow from your strip. Over ten years it has added up to a whole pace of land.
ev.eur_d_boundary.court: Take it to the manor court
ev.eur_d_boundary.court.success: The jurors walked the boundary with a rod and gave you back what was yours.
ev.eur_d_boundary.court.failure: The jurors are the neighbour's kin. The boundary stayed where it was.
ev.eur_d_boundary.stones: Move the boundary stones at night
ev.eur_d_boundary.stones.success: No one noticed. The pace of land came back, and half a pace more.
ev.eur_d_boundary.stones.failure: You were caught with a stone in your hands. Moving a boundary is a worse sin than theft.
ev.eur_d_boundary.forgive: Let it go: neighbours matter more
ev.eur_d_wet_nurse.title: The wet nurse
ev.eur_d_wet_nurse.text: {npc} was born strong and loud. In your circle babies are usually sent to a wet nurse in the country for two years – every respectable family does it.
ev.eur_d_wet_nurse.balia: Send the baby to a nurse in the country
ev.eur_d_wet_nurse.home: Hire a nurse to live in
ev.eur_d_manumission.title: A charter of freedom
ev.eur_d_manumission.text: The lord needs money for war and has announced that serfs may buy their freedom. A clerk is already preparing sealed charters.
ev.eur_d_manumission.borrow: Borrow from neighbours and buy your freedom
ev.eur_d_manumission.borrow.success: The neighbours chipped in. You hold the sealed parchment in your hands: you are free.
ev.eur_d_manumission.borrow.failure: Not enough money could be found. The clerk put the charter back in the chest.
ev.eur_d_levy.title: The muster
ev.eur_d_levy.text: Your lord is mustering men: one man with a spear or bow from every two households. The pay is in silver, with a share of the plunder promised.
ev.eur_d_levy.text.london: The sheriff has proclaimed a muster of archers: the king is going to war and pays threepence a day. Every Sunday you shoot at the butts behind the church anyway.
ev.eur_d_levy.text.florence: The commune is raising its foot militia: each quarter sends its men under its own banner. The city treasury pays.
ev.eur_d_levy.stay.success: You got away with it: they found enough men without you.
ev.eur_d_levy.stay.failure: The bailiff marked you down as a shirker. A fine and sidelong looks.
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.title: Freedom for the village
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.text: The lord is in debt and offers the whole village its freedom at once: no more labour service, no marriage or inheritance fines – just a fixed rent. The village is collecting from every household, and they are waiting at your door for an answer.
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.some: Give half and hope it is enough
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.some.success: It was enough. The lord set his seal to the charter, and the bell rang till evening.
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.some.failure: The sum fell short, the deal collapsed, and the money went to pay the lord's debts.
ev.eur_t_village_franchise.refuse: Refuse: it might be a trick
ev.eur_t_knighted.title: Knighted on the field
ev.eur_t_knighted.text: In the battle you saved your lord's banner when his standard-bearer fell. That evening, before everyone, he touches your shoulder with his sword: he will make you a knight. But the horse and armour are at your own expense.
ev.eur_t_knighted.money: Ask for a reward in coin instead
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.title: A distant kinsman's legacy
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.text: A distant kinsman, a childless knight, has died and named you heir to a small manor. But his nephew has already moved into the house and says the will is forged.
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.claim: Go to law for the manor
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.claim.success: The royal court upheld the will. You are now lord of a manor with a village and a mill.
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.claim.failure: The nephew brought twelve witnesses. You lost the case and made an enemy.
ev.eur_t_inherit_manor.sell: Sell your claim to the nephew
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.title: Denounced
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.text: A neighbour who has owed you money for years has told the inquisitor that you mock the sacrament and never go to confession. You are summoned for questioning.
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.defend: Defend yourself and name the informer's enemies
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.defend.success: The inquisitor heard the witnesses and saw which way the wind was blowing. The charge was dropped.
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.defend.failure: You were held in prison for many months. They let you go, but without half your goods.
ev.eur_t_heresy_accused.penance: Do penance for what you never did
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.title: The robber knight
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.text: On a forest road riders bearing a local knight's arms block the way. He calls it "a toll for protection". Protection from what, he does not say.
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.fight.success: The carters grabbed their cudgels and the knight's men fell back. The taverns talked of it for a long time.
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.fight.failure: They beat you and took more than they had first asked.
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.bluff: Claim you travel under the archbishop's safe-conduct
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.bluff.success: The knight did not dare quarrel with the archbishop and let you pass.
ev.eur_t_robber_knight.bluff.failure: They demanded to see the letter. The lie cost more than the toll.
ev.eur_t_city_fire.title: Fire
ev.eur_t_city_fire.text: At night the bakehouse across the street caught fire. The wooden, thatched houses go up one after another, and the wind carries sparks straight onto your roof.
ev.eur_t_city_fire.goods.success: You carried out the chest and the tools. The house burned, but you kept what mattered.
ev.eur_t_city_fire.goods.failure: A beam fell beside you. You got out with burns and almost nothing else.
ev.eur_t_city_fire.people: Help neighbours bring out the children and the old
ev.eur_t_ransom.title: Prisoner of war
ev.eur_t_ransom.text: In a skirmish you were unhorsed and taken prisoner. Your captor is courteous and feeds you at his own table – and names a ransom that makes your head spin.
ev.eur_t_ransom.parole: Go free on parole and raise the money yourself
ev.eur_t_ransom.parole.success: You raised the money faster than you expected and returned on time. Honour is intact.
ev.eur_t_ransom.parole.failure: The collecting dragged on, interest mounted, and the ransom cost almost everything you had.
ev.eur_t_prince_default.title: The prince will not pay
ev.eur_t_prince_default.text: The prince you lent a great sum for his war has sent a courteous letter: the treasury is empty, the debt will be repaid "when God provides". Your own creditors will not wait.
ev.eur_t_prince_default.sue: Press the case through the courts and the papal legate
ev.eur_t_prince_default.sue.success: The legate applied pressure, and the prince repaid at least part.
ev.eur_t_prince_default.sue.failure: The prince took offence and shut your counting house in his lands.
ev.eur_t_prince_default.customs: Take his wool customs as security
ev.eur_t_prince_default.customs.success: The customs flowed into your coffers – and the prince even thanked you.
ev.eur_t_prince_default.customs.failure: War cut off the trade, the customs dried up, and the debt remained.
ev.eur_t_bishop_patron.title: The bishop notices you
ev.eur_t_bishop_patron.text: The bishop stopped in your parish and saw how quickly you read and reckon. He offers you a place in his household: letters, accounts, errands. A road upward – but also dependence on one man.
ev.eur_t_bishop_later.title: Your patron falls
ev.eur_t_bishop_later.text: Your bishop has quarrelled with the king, and the king's men are listing his property. His servants too are being asked whose side they are on.
ev.eur_t_bishop_later.king: Go over to the king's men
ev.eur_t_treasure.title: Buried treasure
ev.eur_t_treasure.text: The plough caught a clay pot, and old silver coins bearing strange kings spilled out. By law, treasure found in the ground belongs to the king.
ev.eur_t_treasure.hide: Hide it and sell a little at a time
ev.eur_t_treasure.hide.success: The silver went to the money-changer a handful at a time. No one ever knew.
ev.eur_t_treasure.hide.failure: The money-changer told the coroner. The silver was taken and you were fined.
ev.eur_t_treasure.hand: Hand it to the coroner for a reward
ev.eur_t_treasure.church: Give it for a new altar
ev.eur_t_toledo_1391.title: After the riots
ev.eur_t_toledo_1391.text: Since the riots of 1391 preachers walk through the Jewish quarter, and many neighbours have already been baptised. Baptism means keeping your house and trade. Staying in the faith of your fathers means living in fear and paying.
ev.eur_t_toledo_1391.leave: Leave for Italy, where it is calmer
ev.eur_j_dubbing.title: Dubbing
ev.eur_j_dubbing.text: Your years as a squire are behind you. A night's vigil before the altar, and in the morning – spurs, a belt and the blow on the shoulder. But the horse, the armour and the feast for the guests cost a great deal.
ev.eur_j_dubbing.squire: Remain a squire: there is no money
ev.eur_j_knight_service.title: Forty days of service
ev.eur_j_knight_service.text: Your lord summons his vassals: forty days of service on campaign, with your own horse and squire. Instead of serving you may pay shield money.
ev.eur_j_knight_service.serve.success: The campaign was short, the plunder decent.
ev.eur_j_knight_service.serve.failure: Under the walls of a hostile castle a crossbow bolt wounded you.
ev.eur_j_knight_service.excuse.success: Your lord believed you and wished you a swift recovery.
ev.eur_j_knight_service.excuse.failure: Your lord learned you were out hunting those days. A grudge for a long time.
ev.eur_j_monk_scriptorium.title: In the scriptorium
ev.eur_j_monk_scriptorium.text: You have been set at a desk in the scriptorium. You may copy a psalter for the bishop, or the old book of Ovid the librarian keeps on the top shelf. Your fingers freeze, the ink thickens.
ev.eur_j_monk_scriptorium.psalter: Copy the psalter with gilded initials
ev.eur_j_monk_scriptorium.fast: Write quickly and get back to the stove
ev.eur_j_monk_office.title: The cellarer
ev.eur_j_monk_office.text: The abbot offers you the office of cellarer: the barns, vineyards, mills and dozens of the house's tenants. Less prayer, more accounts.
ev.eur_j_mason_lodge.title: The lodge at Cologne
ev.eur_j_mason_lodge.text: At Cologne they have begun a cathedral like none seen before: on the model of Amiens, but taller. Master Gerhard is gathering masons from all over Europe, and he pays well.
ev.eur_j_mason_master.title: Master of the lodge
ev.eur_j_mason_master.text: The old master of the works has taken to his bed. The chapter is looking for someone to trust with the drawings on the plaster floor and dozens of masons. Your name comes up more than any other.
ev.eur_j_mason_master.take.success: The chapter confirmed you. Now your mark will be on the keystone.
ev.eur_j_mason_master.take.failure: The chapter chose a master from Paris instead.
ev.eur_j_banker_prince.title: A royal loan
ev.eur_j_banker_prince.text: An envoy of the English king asks for a huge loan for the war. In return – the right to export wool free of duty, and interest the books will call "a gift".
ev.eur_j_banker_prince.part: Lend a share alongside other companies
ev.eur_j_banker_default.title: The king defaults
ev.eur_j_banker_default.text: The king has declared he cannot pay his debts. Depositors besiege your bench demanding all their money at once.
ev.eur_j_banker_default.absorb: Pay the depositors from your own funds
ev.eur_j_banker_default.run.success: The depositors trusted your word. The bank held.
ev.eur_j_banker_default.run.failure: Panic. They broke your bench – "banca rotta", bankruptcy.
ev.eur_j_wool_fleece.title: Ten years of fleece
ev.eur_j_wool_fleece.text: A Cistercian abbey in the Cotswolds is selling its fleeces ten years in advance – cheaply, but the money is needed now. If scab does not carry off the sheep, it is the deal of a lifetime.
ev.eur_j_wool_fleece.contract.success: The fleece came every year, and cloth prices kept rising.
ev.eur_j_wool_fleece.contract.failure: Sheep scab swept through the flocks. The abbey spreads its hands.
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.title: The ale-taster
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.text: The town ale-taster has come with his mug to check the strength and the price. Barley is dear this year, and you are sorely tempted to water the brew.
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.honest: Brew honestly and sell at the lawful price
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.water.success: The taster smacked his lips and left. The mugs sold briskly.
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.water.failure: The taster spat. A fine, and a trip to the cucking stool by the pond with the whole street watching.
ev.eur_j_alewife_taster.treat: Treat the taster to the best
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.title: A song at the feast
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.text: At the baron's feast the guests call for a song. The baron whispers that he will pay double for a jest at the expense of his neighbour the bishop.
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.satire: Sing a satire on the bishop
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.satire.success: The hall wept with laughter. The baron tossed you a purse.
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.satire.failure: Among the guests was the bishop's nephew. You were shown the gate.
ev.eur_j_minstrel_feast.love: Sing of love – that is always safe
ev.eur_j_minstrel_household.title: A household minstrel
ev.eur_j_minstrel_household.text: The count offers you a place in his household: livery, a seat at table and wages all year round. But you will sing what pleases the count.
ev.eur_j_notary_forgery.title: "Restoring" a charter
ev.eur_j_notary_forgery.text: The abbot asks you to "restore" an ancient charter granting the abbey the forest across the river. The original, he says, was burned, but everyone knows the forest belongs to the house. The baron next door knows otherwise.
ev.eur_j_notary_forgery.forge: Write the "original" in an old hand
ev.eur_j_notary_forgery.forge.success: The charter looks three hundred years old. The court upheld the abbey's rights.
ev.eur_j_notary_forgery.forge.failure: The royal judge noticed that the "ancient" charter mentions a king who is still alive.
ev.eur_j_translator_book.title: An Arabic book
ev.eur_j_translator_book.text: A canon from France orders a translation: Avicenna's Canon of Medicine, or star tables for casting horoscopes. A Jewish scholar reads the Arabic aloud and renders it into Castilian, and you set it down in Latin.
ev.eur_j_translator_book.stars.success: The canon paid handsomely and carried the tables off to Paris.
ev.eur_j_translator_book.stars.failure: Rumours of black magic spread. Clients began to avoid you.
ev.eur_j_translator_book.psalms: Take on a pious treatise instead
ev.eur_j_wanderjahre.title: The journeyman's years
ev.eur_j_wanderjahre.text: The journeymen of your guild go off travelling: from master to master, town to town, learning other men's tricks. A pack, a staff – and years far from home.
ev.eur_j_guild_master.title: A place in the guild
ev.eur_j_guild_master.text: An old master has died, and a place in the guild has fallen vacant. The wardens will admit you – for the entry fee, candles for the guild chapel and a feast for all.
ev.eur_j_reeve.title: Choosing the reeve
ev.eur_j_reeve.text: At Michaelmas the village chooses its reeve. Hands go up for you. The reeve answers to the lord for all the labour services and all the arrears – but is excused his own.
ev.eur_j_captain.title: Captain of the company
ev.eur_j_captain.text: The captain of the company has been killed, and the men want you to lead them: to share out the pay, bargain with the lords and answer for every man.
ev.eur_j_priest_benefice.title: A rich living
ev.eur_j_priest_benefice.text: The baron offers you a rich parish on his estate. Only one condition: overlook whom he lives with in place of his lawful wedded wife, and absolve him without awkward questions.
ev.eur_mv_paris.title: To Paris
ev.eur_mv_paris.text: A merchant you know urges you to come to Paris: the largest city in the West, the king, the court, the university and thousands of customers. A foreign tongue, foreign guilds – and a chance you will never get at home.
ev.eur_mv_toledo_franks.title: Beyond the Pyrenees
ev.eur_mv_toledo_franks.text: The King of Castile is inviting "Franks" to settle in reconquered Toledo: houses, land and special liberties for settlers from beyond the mountains. Wagon trains are already rolling from Burgundy and Gascony.
ev.eur_mv_steelyard.title: The London house
ev.eur_mv_steelyard.text: The Cologne merchants own a hall in London by the Thames: their own yard, warehouses, wharf and liberties from the English king. They need a quick young man there.
ev.eur_mv_factor.title: Factor for the company
ev.eur_mv_factor.text: The company you work for is opening a branch beyond the Alps and needs a factor: to receive wool, issue bills of exchange and write a report every week.
ev.eur_f_confession.title: Easter confession
ev.eur_f_confession.text: The council in Rome has decreed that every Christian must confess to his own priest at least once a year. Your parish priest is very fond of chatting in the tavern.
ev.eur_f_badge.title: The badge
ev.eur_f_badge.text: A new decree orders Jews to wear a sign on their clothes: a yellow cloth wheel or a patch shaped like the tablets of the Law. So that in the street everyone can see at once who you are.
ev.eur_f_badge.exempt: Buy an exemption from the royal official
ev.eur_f_badge.hide: Cover the badge with your cloak
ev.eur_f_badge.hide.success: The watch never once stopped you.
ev.eur_f_badge.hide.failure: A watchman pulled back your cloak. A fine – and the badge is now twice as large.
ev.eur_f_beguine.title: The beguines
ev.eur_f_beguine.text: Behind a wall by the river gate live the beguines: women who take no lifelong vows but live together, pray, weave and tend the sick. Any of them may leave whenever she likes.
ev.eur_f_beguine.join: Go and live with the beguines
ev.eur_f_yeshiva.title: The house of study
ev.eur_f_yeshiva.text: A learned rabbi, a student of the students of the famous Rashi of Troyes, is taking boys: the Talmud with its commentaries, arguments until you are hoarse, candles burning until midnight.
ev.eur_f_disputation.title: A sermon in the synagogue
ev.eur_f_disputation.text: By the king's order a preaching friar has come to the synagogue, and the community must listen. He says the prophets foretold Christ and invites everyone to be baptised on the spot.
ev.eur_f_disputation.argue.success: The friar faltered, and the community repeated your answer for years.
ev.eur_f_disputation.argue.failure: You were accused of insulting the faith. The whole community had to raise the fine.
ev.eur_f_mudejar.title: Mudéjar
ev.eur_f_mudejar.text: You are laying patterned brickwork for a new church – Christians love Moorish work. The contractor hints: be baptised and you will be head mason on double pay.
ev.eur_f_converso.title: Friday candles
ev.eur_f_converso.text: You were baptised long ago, you go to Mass and eat pork in front of the neighbours. But on Fridays your hands still reach to light the candles as they once did. The "Old Christian" neighbours notice everything.
ev.eur_f_converso.candles: Light the candles behind closed shutters
ev.eur_f_converso.candles.success: No one found out. The Friday light remains your secret.
ev.eur_f_converso.candles.failure: A servant informed. A trial began, and half your property went on your defence.
ev.eur_f_vow.title: A vow to a saint
ev.eur_f_vow.text: The illness will not let go. The neighbours advise a vow: bring the saint a wax model of the sick limb and walk barefoot to his relics.
ev.eur_f_vow.vow: Make the vow and go to the relics
ev.eur_f_vow.vow.success: On the way home you felt the fever lift. The wax hand hangs by the shrine among hundreds of others.
ev.eur_f_vow.vow.failure: You reached the relics, but no miracle came.
ev.eur_f_friars.title: The begging friars
ev.eur_f_friars.text: In the square a barefoot friar in a habit tied with a cord is preaching: no money, no house – only poverty, joy and service to the sick. He calls you to the order of Saint Francis.
ev.eur_f_friars.text.toledo: In the Zocodover square a barefoot friar in a habit tied with a cord is preaching: no money, no house – only poverty, joy and service to the sick. He calls you to the order of Saint Francis.
ev.eur_f_friars.join: Give away your goods and go with the friars
